END-TO-END FRONTEND DATA-FLOW trace of a tracking value from URL to wire across every hop; no HIGH/BLOCKER/MED found. Traced chain: utils.js sanitizeTrackingParams -> AuthForm.tsx/SignupForm.tsx state -> useSession.ts magicLink/register variables -> api.ts apiPost/apiMutate -> structure.js allKeysToSnake -> RegistrationsController#sign_up_params. 

SANITIZER OUTPUT SHAPE (utils.js:42-88): returns camelCase keys utmSource/utmCampaign/internalRef, and utmData (nested object of raw utm_* param names). Each field is OMITTED (key absent, so property === undefined) when its param is absent from the URL; utmData present only when >=1 additional utm_* key captured (guard utmDataKeys.length > 0 at :79). Occurrence order is derived from the raw string via queryString.extract().split('&') (:46-56) precisely because query-string v6.1.0 parse() alphabetizes keys -- this correctly satisfies Known-Failure-Pattern #28 and the 10-key cap (:77 slice(0,10)). Surrogate-safe truncation (:34-39) and first-occurrence-of-array (:32) verified; empty-string value -> charCodeAt(-1)=NaN -> returns '' (no crash); valueless '?utm_source' parses to null and passes through as-is. 

CHECK 1 (AuthForm magicLink, :73-87 -> useSession magicLink :56-108): camelCase utmSource/utmCampaign/utmData/internalRef consistent all the way into the variables object at :100-107. CONSISTENT. 
CHECK 2 (SignupForm register, :59-71 -> useSession register :27-54): same four camelCase keys threaded into variables :45-52. CONSISTENT. 
CHECK 3 (AuthForm -> GoogleSSOButton props :131-134 -> hidden inputs): the camelCase->snake_case switch happens at the input name attribute and every one of the 4 maps to the CORRECT backend name: utmSource->name='utm_source' (:66), utmCampaign->name='utm_campaign' (:69), internalRef->name='internal_ref' (:72), utmData->name={'utm_data['+key+']'} Rails-nested (:77). No wrong-name silent-drop. Each renders under the analog guard (typeof x === 'string' && x.length > 0), and utmData is guarded by 'utmData != undefined' (:74) plus a per-key guard (:76). 

CHECK 4 (THE CRITICAL ONE) -- camelCase JSON body vs snake_case controller permit -- RESOLVED DEFINITIVELY: the conversion happens in apiMutate at app/javascript/shared/queryHooks/api.ts:52 (`data: skipKeysToSnake ? variables : allKeysToSnake(variables)`); both register and magicLink call apiPost WITHOUT skipKeysToSnake, so allKeysToSnake IS applied. allKeysToSnake at app/javascript/ats/src/lib/utils/structure.js:94-125 applies lodash snakeCase to every key and RECURSES into nested plain objects (:104), so utmSource->utm_source, utmCampaign->utm_campaign, internalRef->internal_ref, utmData->utm_data, and utmData's inner keys are snakeCased in transit (canonical utm_medium/utm_term/utm_content pass through unchanged; non-canonical utm_content2->utm_content_2 -- matches spec Risk 3). RegistrationsController#sign_up_params (registrations_controller.rb:310) permits exactly the snake_case names ':utm_source, :utm_campaign, :internal_ref, utm_data: {}', and #magic_create reads sign_up_params[:utm_source] etc (:97-100, :110-113). So the values DO persist on the JSON paths -- NO silent drop. CONVENTION PROOF: this is not new behavior for the feature -- pre-existing 'loginIntent' (magicLink variables) is snakeCased to 'login_intent' and read by the SAME sign_up_params permit (:310), and 'referral' (single word, unchanged by snakeCase) is likewise permitted ':referral'. Both ride the identical allKeysToSnake mechanism, proving the house camelCase->snake_case wire convention the four new params follow. 

CHECK 5 (undefined threading): sanitizer omits utmData when absent; AuthForm/SignupForm pass trackingParams.utmData (undefined) into the variables object -- key present, value undefined. allKeysToSnake keeps it as utm_data: undefined; axios JSON.stringify then DROPS undefined-valued keys, so the wire param never arrives and sign_up_params[:utm_data] is nil (column stays nil, no {} fabrication). Same for utmSource/utmCampaign/internalRef when undefined. GoogleSSOButton drops undefined via its guards. Note: a degenerate null-valued inner key (from '?utm_medium') rides JSON as utm_data[utm_medium]=null (JSON.stringify keeps null) but is omitted on the SSO path -- documented/accepted divergence per spec 5.3. Handled everywhere; no crash on undefined. 

CHECK 6 (posthog event names): trackEvent('user_signed_up_client_side') at AuthForm.tsx:91 and SignupForm.tsx:75 -- identical strings, no typo, both fired BEFORE onComplete per spec 5.2/5.5, trackEvent imported from @shared/lib/posthog in both. git grep confirms these are the only two frontend callsites and the server 'user_signed_up' string (registrations_controller.rb:52,190; omniauth_callbacks:35; invites:80) is UNMODIFIED -- distinct name, no collision. posthog.ts change is only the spec-sanctioned window.logger addition in identifyUser (fire + skip paths, spec 5.9); trackEvent gracefully no-ops when posthog not loaded (getPosthog() null guard :43-46) so event firing never blocks the auth flow. 

CROSS-FILE SHAPE CONSISTENCY: GoogleSSOButton Props utmData typed Record<string,any> (:15) and useSession magicLink inline type utmData?: Record<string,any> | null (:80) both accept the sanitizer's object/undefined; register is untyped so no TS friction. No shape mismatch at any boundary. Only exotic-input edge (a '+' or percent-encoded utm key name mis-deduping in the occurrence-order scan at utils.js:51) cannot corrupt values -- the filter guards with parsedParams[key] !== undefined and at worst drops an exotic key from utmData; non-issue for canonical utm_* names and already within the settled sanitizer-edge rulings. No feature defect.
